author: Cydek
quote: ​Instead of pushing the medium forward, GTA 6 stands as a bloated monument to corporate greed and creative stagnation.​After more than a decade and a rumored billion-dollar budget, Rockstar threw everything at hyper-realistic lighting, skin pores, and street clutter, while doing very little to actually evolve the core gameplay. Nothing exposes the true priorities behind this 'immersive world' faster than carving out completed in-game storefronts and holding them hostage behind a $100 Ultimate Edition paywall, all on top of an already steep $80 entry fee.​Behind the scenes, the human cost is just as grim. Even as Take-Two Interactive reaps billions from the launch, the company has already gutted its workforce, from mass corporate layoffs and studio closures like Roll7 and Intercept Games, to laying off a third of the staff at sister studio Firaxis on the very eve of GTA 6's release, and firing over 30 union-organizing Rockstar staffers under the guise of "gross misconduct." Between grueling crunch hours and an employment tribunal over blatant union-busting, the remaining developers who built this record-breaking juggernaut are now left fighting for basic union recognition just to protect their jobs from post-launch cuts and heavy AI replacement.​Even locking a promotional trailer behind a paywall, if only for a short period of time, shows just how disgusting the industry has become and what publishers will normalize next. It is a game that will confirm for every game company CEO, who only sees dollar signs instead of fans and art, that you don't need physical media because GTA 6 didn't need a disc. This will be the catalyst for the end of physical media, stripping players of true ownership and turning a beloved medium into a disposable, digital-only storefront. All of this reflects an industry now completely dictated by casual gun-and-ball gamers who only play annual shooters, sports titles, and expensive AAA releases, sending the message that a massive budget is the only thing that matters in a game, a narrow mindset that inevitably trickles down and homogenizes everything else in the medium.​As for the 99 Metascore, seeing over a hundred critics ignore obvious technical compromises, game-breaking bugs at launch (since patched, to be fair), and largely unchanged gameplay to hand out perfect 10s just shows how broken mainstream games journalism has become. It only reinforces the rumors about the blacklisting of journalists who refuse to give perfect, not even near-perfect, scores. GTA 6 will break every sales record on earth, sure, but all it really proves is that the AAA industry now confuses the most expensive product ever made with the greatest art.
